# Limitations

Written alongside the code rather than bolted on at the end. Where the synthetic data makes
this problem easier than real trade surveillance, and what that means for the numbers in
the README.

## The data is generated by a model, and the detectors assume a similar one

This is the deepest limitation and no amount of engineering removes it. Background notional
is lognormal; the statistical layer scores deviation from a lognormal fit. The detector and
the data-generating process share a family, so the statistical layer's measured performance
is an upper bound that real data would not reproduce.

The graph layer is less exposed to this — its features are structural (who traded with
whom, how often, netting to what) rather than distributional — which is one reason the
project leans on it.

## Anomaly prevalence is roughly 1000x too high

Planted trades are **0.9%** of the dataset. Real market abuse is well under 0.001% of
order flow. Precision degrades roughly linearly with prevalence at fixed recall, so a
detector showing 80% precision here would show low single-digit precision against real
flow at the same threshold. Any precision figure quoted from this project must carry that
caveat.

## No order-level data

Real surveillance leans heavily on orders, not just executions: placements, amendments,
cancellations, order-to-trade ratios, quote stuffing, and time priority. Spoofing and
layering — two of the most important abuse typologies — are essentially invisible in
execution data alone and are therefore **not modelled here at all**. This system detects
three typologies, not the full space.

## Prices are geometric Brownian motion

No jumps, no fat tails, no volatility clustering, no bid-ask bounce beyond a fixed spread,
no order book. The `price_outlier` scenario is consequently easier than its real
counterpart: against GBM, a 3% deviation is unambiguous, whereas real intraday returns
produce 3% moves routinely on illiquid names.

## Account personas are stationary

Each account draws one activity rate, one size distribution and one intraday profile, held
fixed for the whole window. Real accounts change strategy, size up and down, and go quiet.
That stationarity flatters any "relative to this account's own history" feature — which is
most of the statistical layer's feature set. A real deployment would need drift handling
and a rolling baseline that this project does not implement.

## Counterparty matching is synthetic

Wash rings are constructed with an explicit counterparty, which the generator records but
the detection layer is forbidden from reading. The graph layer infers relationships from
co-trading instead. This is the right choice — it is harder and it mirrors what a lit-venue
surveillance system actually sees — but the *inference* still runs against trades that were
generated as clean matched pairs. Real fills fragment across venues, partial fills and
child orders, which would blur the co-trading signal considerably.

## The hard negatives were constructed by the same author as the positives

The discriminators between `coordinated_cluster` (positive) and `event_comovement` (hard
negative) — illiquidity, directional unanimity, no prior history in the name — are real
criteria a surveillance analyst would use. But *I* chose them and then built both scenarios
to differ along exactly those axes. That makes the separation cleaner than reality, where
the two overlap substantially and analysts disagree. The hard negatives prove a detector
isn't naive; they do not prove it would work.

## Single venue, single asset class, no cross-market view

Equities only, one simulated market, no derivatives, no cross-product manipulation (e.g.
moving a cash market to profit on options). Real abuse frequently spans products precisely
because single-product surveillance is common.

## No exchange holidays or auctions

The calendar is weekdays only, and every session is a continuous 09:30–16:00 with no
opening or closing auction. Auctions concentrate a large share of real volume and are a
common venue for manipulation, so their absence removes a whole class of pattern.
